observation: Concept-first discipline (founder research + locked decision on held-vs-inherited + no OAuth app) prevented mid-implementation spec rewrites; concept hard-rule 3 (per-user isolation) and hard-rule 1 (secret never in response) loaded into every task as anchors.

Concept phase required founder + two research passes (t3code model source, MCP/Claude-Code OAuth landscape) before the load-bearing fork (held simple-secret vs inherited token in harness) could be locked. Initial AskUserQuestion rejected because founder wanted evidence first. Research cost: ~3h founder + builder across concept phase.
TDD red-then-green on first pass: 1138c17d red commit → 13 green-phase commits (Tasks 1-8) → 3158 tests PASS on attestation. No re-runs, no rework due to test-discovery.

Code review (Phase 4, prior to AN1 branch) surfaced a real mock-validation trap: unit test for ServiceConnectionResolver used `null as any` for db fixture and never actually called resolver's cross-user logic, leaving the isolation guarantee unproven. Hollow test passed because the mock db returned undefined (all resolves hit the mock), not because the logic worked. Two NOT-DONE rounds: Round 1 wrote real integration tests with cross-user seeds; Round 2 deleted the hollow decoy test (3c727cb1). This is CC-004 in action — hollow production paths survive unit tests; integration tests are the proof boundary.

Architecture plan matched implementation cleanly: 8-task ordered list with dependency graph → 13 commits (some tasks bundled, all ordered respected) → builders never blocked on plan ambiguity. Shared files declared (schema, descriptor, routes, settings page) meant concurrent work by future AL5 (review-surfaces) and AO (credentials) was pre-coordinated.

Discovery probes implemented evidence-first: no code path copies env/command/token into InheritedToolDescriptor; only names/liveness read via `claude mcp list`, `codex mcp list`, `gh auth status --json` (never --show-token). Hard-rule 4 (inherited token never leaked) enforced at type level (no secret field exists) + @lore + review verification. Extensible for new CLIs.

Scope expansion (founder decision, 2026-06-25): pulled AN3's live inherited group into AN1 because concept locked 'inherited' as load-bearing. AN1 now ships the full inherited enumeration via descriptor extension + discovery probes + projection union. AN3 shrinks to enrichment phase. Cost: +3 tasks (descriptor field, discovery, projection) added mid-plan and executed in green phase without replanning. Successful replan, but noted the risk of in-flight scope pulls.

Design story (SettingsConnections.tsx + fixture) was pre-rendered and founder-reviewed in design phase; green phase only confirmed compiled + aligned shared types. Zero design rework. Story published to DSK viewer; variant was marked routine DESIGN-CLASS, no human-design-review gate needed.

Migration 0039 timestamp ordering bug caught at verify time (ac57cb6e): generated migration used `1784900000000` for 0038 and `1784900000000` for 0039, failing the uniqueness invariant. Corrected to `1784900000001` (1ms > 0038). Root cause: migration timestamp generation did not ensure strict ordering. Reflects CC-007 pattern (plan assumed migrationPath works; reality caught at verify). Not a blocker but a sanity-break signal.

Cross-cutting security checklist (SSRF, rate-limit, input trust, cross-user isolation, secret handling) all addressed in architecture plan; builders executed to spec. SSRF partial-by-design (AN1 stores https:// only, full DNS-rebinding block deferred to AN2 outbound-client scope) explicitly recorded in plan as known follow-up, not silent gap. CC-003 pattern: security cases not baked into ACs but added via checklist review and landed cleanly.
